description: Church media server wire protocol. Single source of truth for every client (mobile app, admin web bridge, admin web frontend). Bindings are generated by `npm run gen-protocol` — never hand-edit the generated files.
model: The server is modelled as a device that describes itself: it exposes attributes (state you read and write), commands (actions you invoke), and one event carrying whatever changed. The architecture is borrowed from hardware buses like PCI — enumerate the device, discover what it supports, access everything the same way — but the vocabulary is the device-model one (attribute/command/event) rather than literal registers, because these are named slots, not addressed words.
conventions: Four commands cover everything a client can do: hello (identify), read (get attributes), write (set one attribute), invoke (run one command).
The server sends four things: ready (identity and what it supports, once), state (a patch of attributes that changed), rejected (why a write or invoke was refused), ping (heartbeat).
An attribute is state: it has a value you can read. A command is an action: it takes arguments and has no value. Nothing is modelled as the wrong one — there are no write-only attributes.
One write touches exactly one attribute, so each keeps its own timing and permission rules. Batch writes are deliberately not allowed.
A state patch contains only the attributes that changed. An absent field means unchanged; an explicit null means 'now nothing' (only flow reads as null).
Nothing is inferred from an empty or absent value. Ending something is its own command — stopping a flow is stopFlow, not a null write.
ready lists the attributes and commands this server actually implements. A client must hide controls for anything it does not see, so a server can gain features without a client release.
Every event carries exactly one object payload. No positional arguments, no bare scalars.
The server's state is always authoritative. A write or invoke expresses intent; the result arrives as a state patch.
Times are 'HH:MM' local wall-clock for the current day. If unlockAt is not after lockAt it means the following day.
Nothing here is transport-specific: an event name plus an object payload maps cleanly onto Socket.IO today, or topics later.

PlaybackState.description: Whether the audio deck is sounding

SongType.description: Selectable song in the two-song system users control directly

ConsoleInput.description: Mixing console input. Inputs are independent, not alternatives.

FlowPhase.description: Stage of a running scheduled flow

Access.description: How an attribute may be used

Permission.description: Who may write an attribute or invoke a command

RejectReason.description: Why a write or invoke was refused. Sent only to the client that issued it, so it can explain itself instead of appearing to do nothing.

Track.description: A playable library entry. File paths never leave the server.

durationSec.description: Length in seconds, measured from the file

FlowTrack.description: Which track of a flow is sounding right now

Flow.description: The scheduled flow the server is running

name.description: Display name supplied by the caller

endsAt.description: When the track sequence finishes; null for a lock-only flow

unlockAt.description: When the admin lock releases. Independent of endsAt.

playback.description: Whether the deck is playing. Writing it fades in or out and holds the audio lock for the length of the fade.

volume.description: Output volume. Applies immediately, so it is safe to write continuously while dragging a fader.

song.description: Selected song. Writing it fades out, switches, and restores that song's remembered position, paused.

adminLock.description: Global gate on non-admin writes. Any admin may release it, it survives disconnects, and it is cleared by a restart.

audioLock.description: True while the audio device is mid-transition. Read-only, and it refuses everyone including admins: it guards the device, not permissions.

isAdmin.description: Whether this connection holds admin rights. Per-connection, so it is only ever sent to the client it describes.

flow.description: The scheduled flow the server is running, or null when there is none. Read-only: startFlow and stopFlow change it.

authenticate.description: Claim admin rights for this connection. Success shows up as isAdmin in a state patch; failure comes back as rejected with invalidPassword.

enableConsoleInput.description: Switch a mixing console input on. Not subject to the audio lock. The console reports nothing back, so there is no attribute to read.

startFlow.description: Hand the server a whole scheduled flow to run: it engages the admin lock at lockAt, plays the sequence so it finishes at endsAt (joining mid-sequence if started late), restores the user's song, and releases the lock at unlockAt. One flow at a time.

tracks.description: Track ids in play order. Empty for a lock-only flow.

lockAt.description: When to engage the admin lock. Already past means immediately.

endsAt.description: When the last track must finish. Required when tracks is non-empty.

unlockAt.description: When to release the admin lock. Must be after lockAt.

stopFlow.description: End the running flow now: stop playback, restore the user's song, release the admin lock.

hello.description: First message after connecting. Identifies the client and declares the protocol version it speaks. The server answers with ready, then a full state.

client.description: Human-readable device name shown to the admin, e.g. '본당 태블릿'

read.description: Ask for attribute values, for example after waking from background. Omit fields to read everything.

fields.description: Attribute names to read, or null for all

write.description: Set one attribute. Refused when it is unknown, read-only, out of range, gated by the admin lock, or the device is busy.

invoke.description: Run one command. Refused when it is unknown, the caller lacks permission, or its arguments do not check out.

ready.description: Answer to hello: what this server speaks, what it supports, and the fixed track library. When accepted is false the client is on an incompatible protocol version — it should tell the user to update. State still arrives, but writes and invokes are refused with protocolMismatch.

attributes.description: Attributes this server implements. Hide controls for anything absent.

commands.description: Commands this server implements. Hide controls for anything absent.

state.description: Attributes that changed. Merge into the state held locally — absent fields are unchanged. Sent in full after ready and in reply to read, and as a patch on every change thereafter.

rejected.description: A write or invoke was refused. Sent only to the client that issued it, so it can say why instead of appearing to do nothing.

target.description: Attribute or command name that was refused
